name: Room thermostat plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a wall-mounted room thermostat controlling heating or cooling equipment.
description: A room thermostat is drawn as a small circle or square with a temperature mark, a theta or the letter T, at its wall position. A control link connects it to the heater, valve or air-conditioning unit it controls.

Its position affects comfort: it should not be near heat sources, in direct sunlight or on an external wall. The plan gives the designer a chance to check this, and the mounting height is usually stated in notes.
It does not show whether the thermostat switches mains directly or provides an extra-low-voltage control signal. Wiring type follows the controlled equipment.
readingNotes: Check its position relative to heat sources.
distinction: A schematic temperature switch shows a contact; the plan mark locates the room control.
